rows.title: Assistant Commercial Excellence Manager
rows.descriptionText:
COMMERCIAL EXCELLENCE ASSISTANT MANAGER 

SALES / COMMERCIAL EXCELLENCE 

SW19 - Wimbledon (2 to 3 days per week in the office) 

As Commercial Excellence Assistant Manager, you will play an important role in supporting Coty’s commercial agenda across some of the UK’s most iconic prestige fragrance brands, including Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss.

Working closely with the Commercial Excellence Team and cross-functional partners, you will help turn sales data, retailer performance and brand plans into clear commercial actions that support growth across key customers including Boots, Superdrug and Amazon.

This role offers an exciting blend of commercial analysis, stakeholder management, promotional planning and hands-on execution. You will gain exposure to sales performance, brand meetings, media strategy, retailer planning, launch execution and international collaboration, while building the commercial foundations needed to grow within a fast-paced global beauty business.

THE ROLE 

OPTIMIZE, ENABLE, INNOVATE! 

As our Commercial Excellence Assistant Manager, you will play a key role in supporting the day-to-day commercial excellence agenda for Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss. You will help analyse performance, coordinate commercial activity and support the team in delivering excellent execution across retailers, brands and internal stakeholders.

This role combines sales analysis, commercial planning, stakeholder coordination, promotional execution and modern, data-driven ways of working. You will collaborate closely with Sales, Brand, Media, International teams and retailer partners to support shared commercial goals, while using digital and AI-enabled tools to improve reporting, generate insights and support faster decision making.

What a day in the life of the Assistant Commercial Excellence Manager look like...

Commercial Performance and Sales Analysis 

 Analyse sales performance, retailer data and brand results to identify risks, opportunities and actions. Support regular performance tracking across Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss. Prepare reporting, presentations and recommendations for internal and retailer-facing meetings. Turn data into clear commercial insights that support decision making. Monitor promotional performance and support recommendations on how plans should evolve. Work at pace across multiple priorities, deadlines and stakeholder requests. Use digital and AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, identify patterns and highlight commercial opportunities. Build confidence in explaining performance, insight and recommendations clearly in meetings.

Retailer Planning and Commercial Execution 

 Support day-to-day commercial activity across key retailer partners including Boots, Superdrug and Amazon. Help coordinate promotional plans, customer initiatives and brand activity across retail channels. Support the development and execution of promo plans, including preparation for key planning periods such as September. Work with sales counterparts to understand customer priorities and support strong execution. Partner with internal teams to ensure commercial plans are delivered effectively and on time. Support retailer meeting preparation, including data inputs, performance updates and action tracking. Help ensure customer commitments, promotional plans and commercial actions are followed through. Bring energy, ownership and curiosity to a fast-moving commercial environment.

Brand, Media and Cross-Functional Collaboration 

 Work closely with Brand teams to understand new launches, brand priorities and commercial activation plans. Collaborate with Media teams to understand media strategy and how it connects to promotional and retailer activity. Interact regularly with international teams and cross-functional partners around shared commercial goals. Support Georgia and the wider team on day-to-day priorities while more senior meetings and longer-term projects are led at manager level. Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders across Sales, Brand, Media and Commercial Excellence. Communicate clearly and confidently in meetings, including with more senior stakeholders. Contribute to a collaborative team culture where people work together at pace and with shared ownership. Develop a strong understanding of how brand strategy, retailer execution and commercial performance connect.

YOU ARE A COTY FIT 

As a commercially curious and highly organised professional, you thrive in a fast-paced environment where data, collaboration and stakeholder engagement are key. You enjoy analysing performance, understanding what drives growth and turning information into clear actions.

You are passionate about beauty, eager to learn and motivated by the opportunity to work on iconic brands. You are articulate, personable and confident enough to contribute in meetings, while bringing the right attitude, pace and curiosity to keep developing in a commercial career.

 Around 2 to 4 years’ experience within a commercial, sales, analytics, category, trade marketing, retail, buying, merchandising or customer-facing environment. Experience within Beauty, FMCG, Consumer Goods or Retail would be advantageous. Strong commercial awareness and interest in how brands, retailers and promotional plans drive growth. Strong analytical capability and confidence working with sales data and performance reporting. Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong communication skills and the confidence to speak clearly in meetings. Ability to work with a wide range of stakeholders across sales, brand, media, international teams and retailer partners. A proactive, positive and team-oriented working style. Curiosity, learning agility and passion for the beauty industry. Comfortable working with digital tools, reporting processes and data-driven ways of working. Curiosity about technology, AI and emerging ways of working that can improve commercial performance. Experience supporting a large brand, major retailer, fast-growth business or start-up style environment would be valuable. The drive, energy and ambition to build a successful commercial career within Coty.

If you're ready to help shape the performance of Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss within a leading global beauty business, we want you on our team!

What We Offer

This is a unique opportunity to build strong commercial foundations within a global beauty company, supporting iconic fragrance brands and gaining broad exposure across sales performance, retailer planning, promotional activity, brand launches, media strategy and international collaboration.

You’ll gain experience across commercial excellence, sales analysis, stakeholder management, retailer execution, performance reporting and AI-enabled ways of working, developing the future-focused skills needed to succeed in a modern commercial organisation.

And if you'd like to build a successful career in the beauty industry...

At Coty, we have a strong track record of accelerating careers and creating opportunities well beyond your first role. A career at Coty could take you in many directions, including:

Fast-track commercial progression

 Progress into broader Commercial Excellence, National Account Executive, National Account Manager, Commercial Manager or wider Sales and Commercial leadership roles. Take ownership of increasingly strategic brands, retailers, projects and commercial responsibilities.

Local and international opportunities

 Explore career moves across our regional and global teams. Opportunities to work from Coty locations including New York, Amsterdam, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Sydney, Tokyo and other offices around the world.

Cross-functional career pathways

 Move into exciting adjacent functions such as Marketing, Digital, Category Management, Revenue Growth Management, Ecommerce and broader Commercial leadership roles. Build a diverse skill set across commercial, brand-facing, analytical and retailer-focused disciplines.

Wherever you want your career to go, Coty offers the scale, brands, people and opportunities to help you get there.

You will also have a great benefits package including, amongst others, the following:

 A competitive benefits package to support your health, wellbeing and financial security Private medical insurance with fast access to specialist and mental health support 8% pension fully contributed by Coty Life assurance and income protection for added peace of mind Flexible hybrid working with our Omni-Working model, with up to 50% remote working Generous family-friendly policies including enhanced parental leave, birthday leave, volunteering days and sabbatical options Everyday perks including employee discounts and salary sacrifice schemes Opportunities to get involved in DE&I, sustainability and employee-led initiatives 25 days of holidays + extra 4 days allowance including a day off for your birthday

About Us

Our people make us who we are. They are the brightest minds bringing the boldest ideas to life every day. If you're the kind of person who refuses to settle, if you want to think bigger, learn faster and go further than you ever thought possible, we'd love to hear from you.

Coty is deeply committed to Changing the Conversation around Diversity, Equity & Inclusion to create a more open, inclusive and diverse workplace where all employees can be their authentic selves.

rows.title: Assistant Go to Market Manager
rows.descriptionText:
Role overview:

Assistant Go to Market Manager

London

Currys London Campus at Waterloo

Fixed Term Contract 6 Months

Full Time

Grade 3

At Currys we’re united by one passion: to help everyone enjoy amazing technology. As the UK’s best-known retailer of tech, we’re proud of the service our customers receive – and it’s all down to our team of 25,000 caring and committed colleagues. Working as one team, we learn and grow together, celebrating the big and small moments that make every day amazing.

The role drives the team to ensure we are focusing on the Big Three Priorities: 

1-Capable & Committed Colleagues 

2-Easy to shop 

3-Customers for life 

 

Positioned within the commercial team, you will be right in the centre of a fast paced team, working hand in hand with the buying team, building strong relationships with our biggest suppliers and working closely with all other functions across the Currys business to build, plan and execute the customer and commercial strategy and develop our business for future growth. 

 

This exciting role within the New Business commercial team reports to the Senior Go to Market; you will help support developing the category strategy blue for the category squad. Combining customer and competitor insight along with financial imperatives to ensure the category squad develops a strategy to both maximise CSAT and EBIT. The role will act as a lynchpin between all functional representatives in the squad, pulling together annual, quarterly and in-season initiatives and activities to maximise performance. You will also arm the category buyer to negotiate adequate supplier funding support. 

 

You will need to have good relationship building skills, working closely with the Commercial buying team, Central Planning, Brand and Marketing team, Online team, Services Team and Retail operations and use your influencing skills to secure support to drive the business forward.  

 

Commercial acumen is a must as you will be required to support our analysis of trading performance, providing recommendations of actions to drive our business. Our ideal candidate will be organised and self-motivated in order to prioritise their work whilst having strong attention to detail to ensure everything is right first time. 

 

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to kickstart their career. It is ideal for a candidate who is passionate, organised and has an interest in Technology. Someone who is ambitious and wants to develop their career within a key category for the business. 

Role overview:

As part of this role, you'll be responsible for:

Support the Senior GTM/GTM manager to ensure the squad adequately understands the category landscape, including customers, competitors, trends, financial performance, range performance, threats and opportunities, to support the development of the annual category strategy Support the Senior GTM/GTM Manager to create the blueprint for the annual category strategy, helping define the guiderails for: target KPIs (CSAT, share, EBIT, stock), customer shopping journey, category proposition and the ‘go to market’ plan Work with the Senior GTM/GTM manager and the central planning and brand & marketing function to develop in line with the annual events calendar the ‘Go to market’ strategy and plan for the category, supporting all briefs required for its execution. Support the squad in landing all major initiatives, including major new product launches, new merchandising solutions and changes to the customer journey online and in-store, liaising with relevant supporting departments to deliver right first time. Bringing appropriate analytics and insight from the online and customer team to support decision making related to day to day trading, events and promotions and range changes to ensure the category are making relevant data driven decisions and plans Co-ordinate responses to major marketing briefs across the category in appropriate templates including TV deals, home page nominations, deal lists, CRM requirements, overarching promotions e.g. trade in Work with peer groups to lead cross-functional delivery for all things related to customer journey including PoS, Ticket and online execution briefs. 

You will need:

Good numerical and analytical skills to review data and provide recommendations/actions plans to drive sales, profit and cash  Good planning, organisational and multitasking skills  Can Do Attitude   Inter-personal and communication skills, capable of working cross functionally to achieve the desired results  Customer champion with excellent commercial awareness and understanding of customer needs  Good working knowledge of SharePoint, Teams, Excel, Word and PowerPoint as well as MS Office workflow tools  Experience of working to deadlines  Good presentation and speaking skills 

Qualifications: 

Educated to degree standard or equivalent.  Marketing/Merchandising/Retail/Business Degree.

We know our people are the secret to our success. That's why we're always looking for ways to reward great work. You'll find a host of benefits designed to work for you, including:

Performance related bonusCompetitive pension schemeProduct discounts on the latest techA range of wellbeing initiatives

Why join us:

Join our team and we'll be with you every step of the way, helping you develop the career you want with new opportunities, on-going training and skills for life.

Not only can you shape your own future, but you can help take charge of ours too. As the biggest recycler and repairer of tech in the UK, we’re in a position to make a real impact on people and the planet.

Every voice has a space at our table and we're committed to making inclusion and diversity part of everything we do, including how we strengthen our workforce. We want to make sure you have a fair opportunity to show us your talents during our application process, so if you need any additional assistance with your application please email careers@currys.co.uk and we'll do our best to help.

rows.title: Sr. Manager, Category Strategy & Analysis
rows.descriptionText:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Sr. Manager, Category Strategy & Analysis to be the analytical engine behind the Hims categories — Sexual Health (ED/PE), Testosterone, and Hair. You’ll partner with the GM and Category Directors to shape, prioritize, and drive the initiatives that move the P&L, turning rich analytics and synthesized insight into decisions: what we build, what we launch, and in what order.

This is a strategy seat with real leverage. The Hims portfolio runs on two roadmaps — the tech product roadmap and the treatment development pipeline — and your sizing, models, and prioritization frameworks are what keep both honest, aligned, and defensible in front of leadership.

Reports to the General Manager, Hims. Works day-to-day with Category Directors, finance, product, analytics, and clinical partners.

You Will

Drive Category Strategy & Prioritization

Act as a strategic thought partner to the GM and Category Directors on the category’s biggest levers — acquisition, retention, conversion, and new-treatment launches.Own the analytical backbone of growth initiative management: size opportunities, build prioritization frameworks (impact vs. effort, must-have vs. nice-to-have), and maintain a stack-ranked view across the acquisition, tech product, and treatment development roadmap.Pressure-test business cases before they reach leadership — make the assumptions explicit and the trade-offs visible.Generate ideas and stay on the lookout for opportunities that sit beyond one initiative and would meaningfully drive business value.

Lead in Analytics & Modeling

Use business acumen and justifiable assumptions to build models that drive real decisions — forecasts, scenario analyses, initiative sizing.Create and manipulate dashboards and charts in Looker and Amplitude to draw conclusions, feed models, and make recommendations.Own recurring performance reads — initiative scorecards and WBR inputs across revenue, contribution margin, retention, S2S, and ARPU.Become a close partner to the analytics team, understanding the nuances of data and reporting.

Champion Experiments & Strategic Projects

Develop and deploy experiments with product and analytics; monitor results and recommend iterations and improvements.Act as a leader, key resource, and thought partner in the execution of high-priority one-off projects.Proactively generate hypotheses and solve for problems before they arise; adapt quickly to new organizational priorities.

Support Treatment & Program Launches

Analyze the potential of new treatments, SKUs, and programs — build scenarios and initial forecast models that feed the treatment development roadmap.Conduct market analysis to identify emerging trends and opportunities in men’s health.Help build the launch playbook — map what has to be true for launch success, from clinical and regulatory milestones to go-to-market.

You Have

rows.descriptionText:
About ThredUp

ThredUp is transforming resale with technology and a mission to inspire the world to think secondhand first. By making it easy to buy and sell secondhand, ThredUp has become one of the world's largest online resale platforms for apparel, shoes and accessories. Sellers love ThredUp because we make it easy to clean out their closets and unlock value for themselves or for the charity of their choice while doing good for the planet. Buyers love shopping value, premium and luxury brands all in one place, at up to 90% off estimated retail price. Our proprietary operating platform is the foundation for our managed marketplace and consists of distributed processing infrastructure, proprietary software and systems and data science expertise. With ThredUp’s Resale-as-a-Service, some of the world's leading brands and retailers are leveraging our platform to deliver customizable, scalable resale experiences to their customers. ThredUp has processed over 172 million unique secondhand items from 55,000 brands across 100 categories. By extending the life cycle of clothing, ThredUp is changing the way consumers shop and ushering in a more sustainable future for the fashion industry.

Recognized on TIME Most Influential Companies of 2023, Digiday's WorkLife 50 2023, TIME's Best Inventions of 2022, and Lattice's People Success Awards 2022.

How You Will Make An Impact 

ThredUp is looking for a Manager, CRM Technology & Operations to manage the systems, people, and processes that support personalized customer engagement across email, SMS, push, and in-app messaging.

This role sits at the intersection of lifecycle marketing, marketing technology, data, product, and engineering. You will help execute and evolve our CRM technology ecosystem, with a particular focus on Braze architecture, data and event integrations, audience and segmentation capabilities, cross-channel orchestration, personalization, measurement, and operational scale.

You will also manage the day-to-day work of the individuals responsible for technical CRM production and campaign quality. The ideal candidate is a player-coach who can translate strategy into execution, troubleshoot complex technical issues, configure campaigns and segments, review code, improve production processes, and coach others through change.

In This Role You’ll Get To

Lead the day-to-day work of the CRM technology and technical operations team, supporting campaign production, QA, documentation, tooling, governance, and operating standards.Manage and execute the Braze roadmap, partnering with CRM leadership and cross-functional teams to assess platform capabilities, surface technical risks and tradeoffs, and support prioritization across the CRM technology ecosystem.Partner with Data Engineering, Analytics, Product, and Engineering to improve the flow and activation of customer data from the warehouse, CDP, and other systems.Design and build complex, personalized, cross-channel customer journeys, including campaigns, canvases, segments, templates, and personalization logic across email, SMS, push, and in-app messaging.Assess and improve CRM systems and workflows by identifying capability and ownership gaps, then implementing automation, reusable templates, better tooling, and scalable operating processes.Translate lifecycle strategies into scalable technical solutions, including data requirements, events, attributes, subscription groups, audience logic, personalization, orchestration, experimentation, and measurement.Ensure strong governance across permissions, compliance, deliverability, subscription management, data quality, naming conventions, documentation, and change management.Evaluate and implement new martech, AI, and machine-learning capabilities that improve customer engagement and team productivity.Serve as the primary technical partner to Braze and other marketing technology vendors.

What We’re Looking For

7+ years of experience in CRM technology, marketing operations, lifecycle marketing, marketing systems, or a related technical discipline.Experience leading and developing a CRM operations, marketing technology, email development, or technical production team.Deep hands-on experience with Braze or a comparable customer engagement platform. Braze experience is strongly preferred and may be required depending on the candidate’s background.Strong judgment and communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical audiences.Experience designing and implementing complex, multi-step orchestration across email, SMS, push, and in-app messaging.Experience with marketing systems architecture, including data models, customer events, APIs, integrations, identity, warehouse or CDP activation, and platform governance.A technical foundation as a developer, email engineer, marketing technologist, or CRM systems architect—with the ability to read and write HTML, CSS, Liquid, JavaScript, SQL, or similar languages.Experience hand-coding emails or building CRM campaigns directly, rather than operating solely as a project manager or requirements requester.Strong understanding of audience segmentation, personalization, experimentation, deliverability, consent management, subscription groups, and channel-specific constraints.Proven ability to partner effectively with Data Engineering, Analytics, Product, Engineering, Creative, and Marketing stakeholders.Experience managing complex cross-functional programs and prioritizing a roadmap across competing business needs.Experience with project and workflow management tools such as Jira, Asana, Airtable, or similar platforms.Curiosity about agentic AI, machine learning, adaptive systems, and emerging applications in CRM and marketing technology.

You’ll Be Successful If You

Can move comfortably between strategy and execution—from defining a future-state architecture to troubleshooting a campaign that is failing today.Have led an ESP migration, Braze implementation, data architecture effort, or major CRM platform transformation.Know how to evaluate whether an operational problem is caused by people, process, tooling, approvals, staffing, or system limitations.Are willing to challenge inefficient ways of working while bringing the team along.Build durable systems: clear documentation, reusable workflows, scalable templates, strong governance, and measurable success criteria.Understand how CRM technology can support both near-term revenue and long-term retention, personalization, and customer value.

At ThredUp, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. This role pays between $ 175,000 and $200,000, and your actual base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

Many ThredUp employees also have the opportunity to own shares of ThredUp stock, ThredUp employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, as well as a discount when purchasing ThredUp stock if voluntarily participating in ThredUp’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Subject to eligibility requirements, you’ll also receive other benefits: Comprehensive medical & dental coverage, vision, 401k, life and disability insurance.

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

rows.title: Principal Data Engineer
rows.descriptionText:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.
About The RoleWe're hiring a Principal Data Engineer to set the technical direction for data at Hims & Hers. This is the most senior individual contributor role in Data Platform Engineering (DPE), and the scope is deliberately larger than DPE: the architecture you define determines how Software Engineering, Analytics Engineering, and Data Science build on data for millions of patients across our telehealth, prescription, and wellness products.The platform runs on GCP BigQuery, Airflow on Astronomer/EKS, dbt, Confluent Kafka, Databricks Delta Lake, and Terraform/OpenTofu. Two foundational pieces are being built from scratch right now: a streaming platform and a lower environments strategy. The most consequential open question is whether streaming stays scoped to analytics or extends into production and model evaluation paths that other teams depend on. That call is yours to make, and the company will live with it for years.We have Staff engineers who own domains and ship them well. What we don't have is a single person accountable for whether those domains add up to a coherent platform, and for whether the bets we're placing now still look right in five years. That's this role.
You WillThe multi-year platform architecture. Ingestion, streaming, orchestration, transformation, and serving as one system rather than five. You decide what we build, what we buy, what we deprecate, and in what order.
The streaming bet. Whether Kafka to Flink to BigQuery stays an analytics pipeline or becomes production infrastructure, and what that commits us to operationally, financially, and organizationally. You architect for the answer you choose.
The contracts between organizations. The interfaces, service boundaries, and data contracts governing how other teams consume from and write into the platform. Where your standards end and another org's autonomy begins is a boundary you define with the VP of Data, not one handed to you.
What "trustworthy data" means here, and who is on the hook for it. You define the quality and freshness guarantees the platform makes, the tiering that determines which datasets get them, and the accountability model when they're missed. Staff engineers build the detection, validation, and alerting systems. You decide what we promise, to whom, and at what cost.
The economics of the platform. The design decisions that determine what data costs us at scale (storage and compute strategy, reservation model, orchestration footprint) and the accountability framework that keeps consumption honest as more teams build on it. You set the framework. You don't tune every query.
The self service strategy. What capabilities let Analytics Engineering and Data Science move without waiting on DPE, what guardrails keep that from breaking production, and how the platform stops being a bottleneck as demand grows faster than headcount.
The standards the discipline runs on. Testing, CI/CD, observability, schema governance, and infrastructure as code practice, adopted by teams that don't report to you because the standards are good rather than because you can compel them.
Architecture Review. You chair it, and you are the decision maker of record for cross team, multi system, and cost impacting changes, including ones that touch systems you don't own.
The seams between data and everything else. ML and Data Science readiness, HIPAA and PHI compliance posture with Legal and Security, and infrastructure hardening with DevOps. Nobody else is looking at all four at once.
The written record. ADRs, design docs, and RFCs that other teams cite as the reference. If a decision only exists in your head, you haven't finished making it.
The technical ceiling of the org. Mentorship, design review, and hands-on pairing that makes Staff and Senior engineers better. Part of how you'll measure your impact is the volume of decisions you no longer have to make yourself.You stay hands-on throughout. You write and review production code, and you're in the room for platform-level P1s, driving the systemic fix rather than owning the runbook. This is a technical authority role, not an advisory one.


You Have15+ years building and owning data platform architecture, with a record of decisions whose consequences you stayed to live with, ideally across multiple companies or multiple platform generationsEvidence you've set technical direction for organizations you didn't manage, and got adoption through credibility rather than reporting linesExperience defining the edges of your own architectural authority. Ambiguity about where your mandate ends should not stall youDeep GCP and BigQuery expertise, plus real operational fluency in AWS (our Airflow runs on EKS). Multicloud is the job here, not a bonusModern data stack at platform scale: governing dbt across teams, Airflow/Astronomer, Kafka/Confluent, Databricks/Spark, Fivetran, and reverse ETL or activation platforms such as HightouchEvent streaming in production at scale, including Schema Registry, data contracts, consumer lag management, and delivery semantics along with what they actually cost. You raise the bar on production pipeline code by reviewing it, not by talking about itWriting that creates alignment across organizations. Your design docs are where decisions get made, not summaries of decisions already made elsewhere
Preferred QualificationsDatabricks, Unity Catalog, and Delta Lake in production at scaleCDC patterns and Flink for real-time processing, particularly where streaming infrastructure served both analytics and production or model serving paths across multiple teamsPySpark and SparkSQL for large-scale batch and streaming workloadsA BigQuery to Databricks Lakehouse migration, or an equivalent warehouse migration you led end to endMLOps partnership: model training pipelines, feature stores, experimentation infrastructure, or the data foundations behind AI-driven product featuresGo or Python service development for Kafka producers and consumersDirect-to-consumer healthcare or telehealth with HIPAA and GDPR obligationsSOX compliance controls in a data engineering context

rows.title: Lead Data Scientist, Inference
rows.descriptionText:
About Strava

Strava is the app for active people. With over 200 million athletes in more than 185 countries, it’s more than tracking workouts—it’s where people make progress together, from new habits to new personal bests. No matter your sport or how you track it, Strava’s got you covered. Find your crew, crush your goals, and make every effort count. Start your journey with Strava today.

Our mission is simple: to motivate people to live their best active lives. We believe in the power of movement to connect and drive people forward.

About This Role

The Data Science team at Strava works across the organization to find solutions to the highest-leverage, and often the most challenging, problems facing the business. We use machine learning, causal inference, and measurement systems to synthesize Strava’s unique data assets into models, metrics, and recommendations that our leadership team can act on with confidence.

This is a strategic individual contributor role that works to link the efforts of our product and marketing teams to tangible outcomes for our athletes and for our business. You’ll develop novel scientific approaches to measuring out business, developing the necessary causal frameworks and models, and help teams develop and evolve our metric strategy to ensure development across the company points toward the highest-leverage outcomes

We follow a flexible hybrid model that translates to more than half of your time on-site in our San Francisco office — three days per week.

What You’ll Do:

Design measurement strategies for Strava's most complex initiatives, applying experimental and quasi-experimental methods (geo testing, difference-in-differences, IV, synthetic control, etc..) to quantify business outcomesExpand Strava’s understanding of the relationship between user experiences and business performance and evolve org-wide metric strategies, connecting product development and marketing efforts to high quality resultsLead deep root-cause investigations into business and product performance, developing novel approaches for problems that don't have an established playbook. Serve as a domain expert in inference for the data team horizontally, reviewing measurement designs and raising the bar for causal evidence quality across DS, Analytics, and cross-functional partners

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

5+ years of experience in data science or a related quantitative domain with experience owning measurement strategies and employing both experimental and quasi-experimental methodsDepth in causal inference methods and their real-world failure modes, with the judgment to know when each approach is credible and when it isn't. Strong SQL proficiency and comfort writing Python for statistical data processingPython proficiency, with comfort writing production-quality code for statistical analysis and experiment toolingAbility to communicate quantitative findings as a clear narrative to technical and non-technical partners in product, finance, and senior leadership

For information on benefits, please click here.

Why Join Us?

Movement brings us together. At Strava, we’re building the world’s largest community of active people, helping them stay motivated and achieve their goals.

Our global team is passionate about making movement fun, meaningful, and accessible to everyone. Whether you’re shaping the technology, growing our community, or driving innovation, your work at Strava makes an impact.

When you join Strava, you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a movement. If you’re ready to bring your energy, ideas, and drive, let’s build something incredible together.

Strava builds software that makes the best part of our athletes’ days even better. Just as we’re deeply committed to unlocking their potential, we’re dedicated to providing a world-class, inclusive workplace where our employees can grow and thrive, too. We’re backed by Sequoia Capital, TCV, Madrone Partners and Jackson Square Ventures, and we’re expanding in order to exceed the needs of our growing community of global athletes. Our culture reflects our community. We are continuously striving to hire and engage teammates from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives because we know we are a stronger team together.

In keeping with the values of Strava, we make all employment decisions including hiring, evaluation, termination, promotional and training opportunities, without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, physical handicap, mental disability, medical condition, disability, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight.

Our Growth Product Team

Noom's Growth Product team owns the acquisition experiences that introduce millions of people to healthier habits every year. We build and continuously optimize the buyflows, landing experiences, and self-service tooling that turn curiosity into commitment — using data, experimentation, and increasingly, agentic AI tools to move faster than teams twice our size. We're a small, scrappy group that believes the best growth work happens when builders can go from idea to live experiment without waiting in an engineering queue.

About The Role

We're looking for a Growth Product Builder to define, build, test, and analyze new buyflow ideas to drive growth using our internal self-service buyflow building tool, Noom Flow Builder. Through your work, you’ll also shape Flow Builder's own roadmap, partnering directly with engineering to expand what the tool can do, first for Growth and eventually for the broader company.

You'll work closely with the VP of Growth Product and the Noom Flow Builder engineering team, with real opportunity to grow your scope — either by building out a team of buyflow builders, or by deepening your influence on the platform's roadmap.

You Will

Define, spec, and build new buyflow variants directly in Noom Flow Builder, our internal agentic buyflow toolLaunch and manage experiments to test buyflow ideas, from hypothesis through analysisIndependently monitor, measure, and iterate on live flows using analytics toolsPartner with the Noom Flow Builder engineering team to identify and prioritize improvements to the toolBring a builder's perspective to the platform roadmap as adoption grows across the companyCommunicate experiment plans, progress, and results clearly to the Product teamCollaborate with Marketing and other Growth Product managers on shared acquisition prioritiesStay current on self-service growth tooling and agentic AI coding tools to keep buyflow development fast and high quality

About You

If you're interested in shaping the future of health by building the acquisition experiences that turn curiosity into lasting habits, this role may be for you!

You Have

What You'll Earn And Enjoy

Pay that reflects your impact. Compensation benchmarked to the market and shaped by your impact and value.Investment in your future. A 401(k) with company match to help you build long-term financial security.Time to truly recharge. Stock awards, a performance-based bonus, and exclusive access to Noom's products, so you can grow with us, win with us, and enjoy what we build.

This role is eligible for our Princeton (preferred) or NYC office locations, operating on a hybrid schedule (2 days per week on-site).

Noom is a leading whole-person health platform on a mission to help people live better, longer. We combine personalized medication with the science of behavior change and psychology, to help people build lasting habits and live longer, healthier lives. With nationally-recognized, holistic programs spanning weight, diabetes prevention, GLP-1 support, menopause, longevity, and more, we serve millions through health plans, employers, and direct-to-consumer offerings. As a trailblazer in the world of health and wellness, Noom makes healthy living easy, fun, and deeply rewarding.

We're more than a health tech company—we're a movement. This belief extends to our culture: we empower our people to think big, act boldly, and take pride in their contributions to shaping the future of health. We've been named one of the Best Places to Work by Inc., Fortune, Glassdoor, and Quartz—including honors for technology and diversity.

Join us in shaping the future of health. You'll be part of a passionate, mission-driven team working to make the world a healthier place—one habit at a time.

rows.title: Lifecycle Marketing Lead - Growth
rows.descriptionText:
At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock human performance. WHOOP empowers its members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.

WHOOP is looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Lead – Growth to own lifecycle strategies across Apparel & Accessories, Refer a Friend, and the promotional calendar. This role is ideal for a highly analytical marketer who can move seamlessly between strategy and execution. You’ll dig into performance and member data to identify opportunities, form hypotheses, and translate insights into action. With an experimentation-first mindset, you’ll test and learn quickly, continually finding new ways to engage members and drive measurable business impact.

The ideal candidate is a member-centric, data-driven marketer who can move seamlessly between strategy and execution. You know how to turn insights into action, test and learn quickly, and continually find new ways to engage members and drive measurable business impact.

Own the lifecycle strategy and performance for Apparel & Accessories, driving product discovery, cross-sell, repeat purchase, and incremental bookings.Own the Refer a Friend lifecycle strategy, identifying and testing opportunities to increase awareness, participation, and referral activity.Lead the lifecycle promotional calendar, defining how promotional moments come to life across owned channels while balancing growth goals with the member experience.Translate member behavior, performance data, and business insights into strategies, experiments, and growth opportunities.Own the test-and-learn cycle from hypothesis through measurement, interpreting experiment results and using learnings to determine what to scale, iterate, or stop.Develop coordinated experiences across email, SMS, in-app, and other owned channels throughout the member journey.Partner cross-functionally across the Growth, Marketing, Creative, Analytics, and Commercial teams to bring high-impact lifecycle initiatives to life.

Experience with Iterable, Amplitude, or Hightouch is a plus.Strong cross-functional collaboration and project management skills, with the ability to independently own multiple programs from strategy through execution.Experience in a subscription, e-commerce, or consumer technology business is a plus.

This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.

Two Sigma is a leading quantitative investment management and trading firm. The company applies a scientific approach to investing, combining cutting-edge technology, artificial intelligence, data science, and quantitative research with rigorous human inquiry to capitalize on market opportunities and deliver alpha for investors.

Our team of engineers, quantitative researchers and data scientists looks beyond the traditional to test hypotheses and develop creative solutions to some of the world’s most complex economic problems.

In this role, you will run the full research process, applying rigorous scientific methods to design sophisticated investment models for trading global markets. You will also help lead portfolio management — overseeing billions in risk capital, managing risk, generating new alpha through research, and driving new product development.

rows.descriptionText:
Position Summary

Two Sigma is a leading quantitative investment management and trading firm. The company applies a scientific approach to investing, combining cutting-edge technology, artificial intelligence, data science, and quantitative research with rigorous human inquiry to capitalize on market opportunities and deliver alpha for investors.

Our team of engineers, quantitative researchers and data scientists looks beyond the traditional to test hypotheses and develop creative solutions to some of the world’s most complex economic problems.

We are applying large language models and transformer-based architectures to problems where ground truth is delayed, noisy, and non-stationary. Our systems generate code, run experiments, and iterate autonomously, and we are looking to go beyond supervised fine-tuning.

We are hiring a Post-Training Research Scientist to build RLHF, DPO, and reward modeling capabilities from the ground up. This is a greenfield role: you will define the infrastructure, research agenda, and evaluation frameworks for aligning LLMs to sophisticated, multi-step workflows in a domain where the reward signal is fundamentally different from existing research on human preference or deterministic task completion.

This hire will help own methodology across training, fine-tuning, context management, and model evaluation. You will shape not only the post-training capability but the broader research direction of the team.

You Will Take On The Following Responsibilities

Lead post-training efforts for LLMs applied to financial time series and quantitative reasoningDesign and execute RLHF, DPO, and related alignment methods at scale, including deployment of substantial compute budgets (O($100mm))Build infrastructure for preference data collection, reward modeling, and policy optimization on financial datasetsDrive research agenda connecting post-training methods to quantitative finance applicationsCollaborate with quant researchers to define task distributions and evaluation frameworksUnblock production systems dependent on post-training capabilities

You Should Possess The Following Qualifications

BS or equivalent work experience in Science, Technology, Engineering or Math (an MS is a plus).Minimum 1 year of experience required; 1-10 years of experience preferred (ideally 1-5 years) at a frontier AI lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, Meta FAIR, or equivalent)Shipped post-training systems in production: RLHF, DPO, RLAIF, or related methodsDeep understanding of distributed training infrastructure: multi-node GPU clusters, training stability, checkpointingTrack record managing large-scale compute: budgeting, experiment design, ablationsPublications or demonstrated expertise in alignment, preference learning, or reward modelingHands-on implementation skills: PyTorch/JAX, distributed frameworks (DeepSpeed, FSDP, etc.)

Core Benefits: Fully paid medical and dental insurance premiums for employees and dependents, competitive 401k match, employer-paid life & disability insurancePerks: Onsite gyms with laundry service, wellness activities, casual dress, snacks, game roomsLearning: Tuition reimbursement, conference and training sponsorshipTime Off: Generous vacation and unlimited sick days, competitive paid caregiver leavesHybrid Work Policy: Flexible in-office days with budget for home office setup

rows.title: Regional Marketing Manager, Brazil
rows.descriptionText:
Overview

Working at Atlassian

Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.

Responsibilities

Atlassian is at an inflection point. We built one of the most successful product-led growth engines in enterprise software — millions of teams adopted our tools bottom-up, without a single sales call. Now we're in the middle of a deliberate, high-stakes evolution: taking that massive installed base and building an enterprise go-to-market motion on top of it. AI is accelerating everything. Our products (Jira, Confluence, Loom, Rovo) are becoming an AI-powered platform — the connective tissue for how the world's best teams plan, build, and deliver.

This role exists to bring that story to life in-market and turn it into pipeline for sales.

We're looking for a Regional Marketing Manager to own the marketing strategy and pipeline outcomes for LATAM, with a primary focus on Brazil. Our job is simple: generate pipeline for sales. Everything we do — every event, campaign, partner activation, and regional program — is measured by whether it creates and accelerates opportunities for our sales teams.

You'll work alongside sales, PMM, demand gen, events, and partner marketing — but you are the one accountable for understanding why the region is or isn't hitting its number, and for driving the response. We're looking for someone who thinks like a business owner, not a program operator.

In This Role You Will

Own a regional pipeline target and be directly accountable for generating and accelerating pipeline for the sales team in LATAMDiagnose performance gaps — when the region is behind, you own figuring out why and recommending the change in approachBring Atlassian's AI and platform transformation story to life in-market — translating global narratives into locally resonant proof points, customer stories, and campaign themesBuild and execute the regional marketing strategy in close partnership with sales leadershipLeverage AI tools (Rovo, Atlassian Intelligence, third-party platforms) to inform strategy, personalize at scale, and accelerate campaign development and performance analysisInfluence and shape priorities across central teams (demand gen, PMM, brand, events) based on what your region actually needsTranslate regional market intelligence into recommendations that inform global campaign strategy, content priorities, and investment decisionsBe the voice of LATAM inside the marketing organization — ensure regional priorities are represented in planningPartner with regional sales leaders to align on target accounts, segment priorities, and go-to-market motionsCoordinate across ABM, demand gen, events, and partner marketing to deliver a cohesive, locally relevant marketing mixWork with partner marketing and channel partners to drive co-marketing initiatives that amplify regional reachManage the regional activity calendar and ensure all motions ladder up to the pipeline planMeasure, analyze, and report on regional performance to marketing and sales leadershipOversee adaptation of global content and campaigns to ensure relevance — and flag when global programs won't land in-market


Qualifications

On the first day we'll expect you to have:

6-7+ years in B2B marketing with a regional or market-level focus (field marketing, demand gen, or regional marketing)Experience generating pipeline for a sales organization — you've owned a number, built programs to hit it, and can speak to how your work directly created revenue opportunitiesStrong AI fluency — you actively use AI tools in your marketing workflow (content generation, audience insights, campaign optimization, analytics) and can articulate how AI changes the marketing playbookGenuine curiosity about how AI is transforming enterprise software and the ability to translate that into compelling marketing narrativesStrong strategic thinking: you can diagnose a performance gap, build a hypothesis, and recommend a course of actionTrack record of influencing cross-functional teams — not just coordinating with themSelf-starting tendencies with an ability to drive projects forward without waiting for permissionDeep understanding of B2B buying cycles and how marketing motions map to pipeline stagesComfort with data: you use pipeline and campaign performance data to make decisions, not just report on themExperience with marketing automation and CRM (Salesforce & Marketo a plus)Brazilian Portuguese native essential


It's a Plus If You Have

Experience marketing platform or enterprise transformation products to C-suite buyersFamiliarity with both product-led growth (PLG) and sales-led enterprise go-to-market motions — and an understanding of how they complement each otherFamiliarity with Atlassian's product suite and the "system of work" value propositionBackground in a high-growth B2B SaaS company navigating a major product or positioning shift


About Our Team

We are Regional & Partner Marketing — a global team of business owners, not program operators. We're building a new kind of regional marketing function where every marketer is a strategist, an advocate for their market, and accountable for pipeline. If you want to be part of shaping how one of the world's most iconic software companies tells its next chapter — market by market, customer by customer — this is the team.

Compensation

At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. To support this goal, the baseline of our range is higher than that of the typical market range, but in turn we expect to hire most candidates near this baseline. Base pay within the range is ultimately determined by a candidate's skills, expertise, or experience.

Role

In the United States, we have three geographic pay zones. For this role, our current base pay ranges for new hires in each zone are:

Zone A: $127,800 USD - $166,850 USD

Zone B: $115,200 USD - $150,400 USD

Zone C: $106,200 USD - $138,650 USD

This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.

Please visit go.atlassian.com/payzones for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

Benefits & Perks

Atlassian offers a wide range of perks and benefits designed to support you, your family and to help you engage with your local community. Our offerings include health and wellbeing resources, paid volunteer days, and so much more. To learn more, visit go.atlassian.com/perksandbenefits .

About Atlassian

At Atlassian, we're motivated by a common goal: to unleash the potential of every team. Our software products help teams all over the planet and our solutions are designed for all types of work. Team collaboration through our tools makes what may be impossible alone, possible together.

We believe that the unique contributions of all Atlassians create our success. To ensure that our products and culture continue to incorporate everyone's perspectives and experience, we never discriminate based on race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, or marital, veteran, or disability status. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

To provide you the best experience, we can support with accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process. Simply inform our Recruitment team during your conversation with them.

To learn more about our culture and hiring process, visit go.atlassian.com/crh .

rows.title: Senior Manager, Fraud
rows.descriptionText:
At Underdog, we make sports more fun.

Our thesis is simple: build the best product for sports fans and we will win the space. Founded in 2020, we're one of the fastest-growing sports companies ever, and there's still so much left to do. We've built and scaled products across fantasy sports, sports betting, and prediction markets, all united in one app that's seamless, intuitive, and actually fun to use.

Underdog isn't for everyone. One of our core values is give a sh*t. The people who win here are the ones who care, push, and perform. We're remote-first by design, but highly collaborative with regular in-person gatherings that help teams build, iterate, and move fast together.

Got that dog in you? Join us.

After all, winning as an Underdog is more fun.

What you'll do:

Underdog is looking for a Senior Manager, Fraud to own and grow our fraud program. This is a builder's role: you will take an evolving fraud landscape and turn it into strong, well-instrumented rules, controls, and decisioning strategies. You will work across the full fraud lifecycle, partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Data/Analytics, and drive ambiguous problems through to implementation.

This role is built around fraud expertise and judgment. Success will be measured by the strength of the fraud program you build and your ability to influence and align teams across the company.

Own and grow the fraud program - find the gaps in how we detect, decide, and investigate fraud today, then build or fix what closes themLead and develop a high-performing fraud team - set clear priorities, strengthen fraud judgment, and hold the team accountable for measurable outcomesDesign the decisioning strategy - build the rules, signals, and logic that carry a case from detection through mitigation and measurementRun the tools yourself - configure and tune platforms like Sift, Sardine, or similar to sharpen detection accuracy and cut false positivesPartner directly with Product and Engineering to scope, build, and ship new fraud capabilities and controlsWork the data - spot fraud trends, test hypotheses, and prove out what your controls are actually doing, alongside Data/AnalyticsPush automation forward - look for every chance to put AI, automation, and new data sources to work on fraudDrive it across teams - take on ambiguous fraud problems and carry them through to implementation, pulling in Product, Engineering, Data, Operations, and Legal/Compliance as needed

Who you are:

You have 5+ years in fraud, risk, payments risk, or a similar functionYou've led and developed fraud professionals, setting clear priorities, strengthening their judgment, and holding the team accountable for resultsYou're hands-on with fraud tooling - platforms like Sift, Sardine, or similar decisioning toolsYou know the full fraud lifecycle inside and out, and can design rules, controls, signals, and decisioning strategies across itYou're fluent in data - spotting trends, forming hypotheses, and measuring performance alongside Data/AnalyticsYou've partnered directly with Product and Engineering to build or ship fraud capabilitiesYou think AI and automation first, always looking for new tools and data to applyYou can take an ambiguous problem and drive it to implementation across multiple teams

Our target starting base salary range for this position is between $140,000 and $175,000, plus target equity. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors including relevant experience, skills and expertise, interview performance, and other market considerations.

What we can offer you:

Unlimited PTO for full-time employees (we're extremely flexible with the exception of the first few weeks before and into the NFL season)16 weeks of fully paid parental leaveHome office stipendA virtual-first culture, but we come together a few times per year in person for offsites, trainings, hackathons, and moreSlack reactions for every occasion401k with up to 5% employer matchCompany paid health, dental, vision plan options for employees and dependents, FSA, and moreOpportunity to celebrate your favorite sports teams through local meetups and company-sponsored eventsClaude and ChatGPT enterprise accounts

Underdog is an equal opportunity employer and doesn't discriminate on the basis of creed, race, sexual orientation, gender, age, disability status, or any other defining characteristic.
